ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Martinho made a bicolor kite with six pieces of a thin strip of bamboo. Two pieces were used for the diagonals, which are perpendicular. The other four pieces were used to connect the middle points on the sides of the kite, as shown in the picture. What is the ratio between the blue and yellow parts of the kite?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows an outer kite-shaped quadrilateral. Its four corner regions are colored yellow, and a central quadrilateral is colored blue. The blue quadrilateral has its vertices on the sides of the outer kite, and the black bamboo strips include the kite’s diagonals plus the four segments forming the boundary of this central quadrilateral. Reasoning: The text states that the four non-diagonal bamboo pieces connect the middle points of the sides of the kite, so the blue quadrilateral is the quadrilateral formed by joining consecutive side midpoints of the outer quadrilateral. By Varignon's theorem, the midpoint quadrilateral of any quadrilateral has exactly half the area of the original quadrilateral. Therefore the blue area is half of the kite. The remaining yellow regions make up the other half. Hence blue : yellow = 1 : 1, so the ratio is 1.

method.method_draft: Read the picture as an outer kite whose four side midpoints have been joined, forming the central blue quadrilateral; the four corner triangles outside that midpoint quadrilateral are yellow. From the text, use that the four non-diagonal bamboo pieces connect the midpoints of the sides. Apply Varignon's theorem: in any quadrilateral, the quadrilateral formed by joining consecutive side midpoints has area exactly half the area of the original quadrilateral. Therefore the blue midpoint quadrilateral occupies half the kite, and the remaining yellow corner regions also occupy half. The blue-to-yellow area ratio is 1.

method.method_draft: Read the image as a kite with perpendicular diagonals and with a blue inner quadrilateral whose vertices are the midpoints of the four sides; the yellow parts are the four outer corner triangles. From the text, take the diagonals to be perpendicular. Place the diagonal intersection at the origin, with the horizontal diagonal endpoints at (-b,0) and (a,0), and the vertical diagonal endpoints at (0,c) and (0,-d). The outer kite area is half the product of its perpendicular diagonals: ((a+b)(c+d))/2. The side midpoints are (-b/2,c/2), (a/2,c/2), (a/2,-d/2), and (-b/2,-d/2), forming a rectangle with width (a+b)/2 and height (c+d)/2. Its area is ((a+b)(c+d))/4, exactly half the kite. Thus blue area equals yellow area, so the ratio is 1.
